title: The Erdberg House to the Stone at Alpbach: the Wave Equation and the Cities That Took Him In
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Vienna, born in Erdberg
stops.date_confidence: attested; German Wikipedia and MacTutor agree on 12 August 1887 in Vienna-Erdberg
stops.campa: In the Erdberg district on the eastern edge of Vienna a son is born to Rudolf Schrödinger, a linoleum manufacturer who keeps up botany as a serious amateur, and to Georgine Emilia Bauer, called Emily. They name him Erwin Rudolf Josef Alexander. He is their only child. The factory carries the household comfortably through the last decades of Austria-Hungary: tutors, books, a garden, an unhurried childhood in a capital that believes itself permanent. He is tutored at home and does not see the inside of a school until he is about ten.
suggested_refs: The Erdberg district of Vienna, birthplace and site of the family linoleum concern

stops.name: Vienna, the Akademisches Gymnasium
stops.date_confidence: attested to the years 1898-1906 by MacTutor (home tutoring to about ten, then the Gymnasium, graduating 1906); month and day defaulted to the start of a school year
stops.campa: He enters the Akademisches Gymnasium in the first district and stays eight years. The curriculum is Greek and Latin grammar, mathematics, physics, German literature, and he takes all of it seriously, the grammars as much as the equations. What he refuses is memorization for its own sake, the dates and incidental facts a schoolboy is meant to swallow whole. On his own account he reads the German dramatists, and resents having them taken apart line by line in class. He graduates in 1906 and crosses the city to the university.
stops.quote: I was a good student in all subjects, loved mathematics and physics, but also the strict logic of the ancient grammars, hated only memorising incidental dates and facts. Of the German poets, I loved especially the dramatists, but hated the pedantic dissection of their works.
stops.quote_source: Schrödinger on his schooldays, quoted in the MacTutor biography
suggested_refs: The Akademisches Gymnasium, Beethovenplatz, Vienna

stops.name: Vienna, the doctorate on moist insulators
stops.date_confidence: attested; MacTutor gives the doctorate as awarded 20 May 1910
stops.campa: He studies physics at the University of Vienna under the men who carry Boltzmann's statistical tradition: Franz Exner in the laboratory, Friedrich Hasenöhrl in theory. On the twentieth of May 1910 he takes his doctorate for a dissertation on the conduction of electricity across the surface of insulators in moist air. It is an experimentalist's problem, measured in damp rooms, and nothing in it forecasts anything. He stays on as Exner's assistant from 1911, running the practical classes and taking on the statistical habit of mind of the place. His first paper of any weight, in 1914, extends Boltzmann.
suggested_refs: The physics institute of the University of Vienna under Franz Exner

stops.name: Seeham, measuring the radioactivity of open air
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1913 (en.wikipedia, which misplaces Seeham in Switzerland; it is in Salzburg, Austria); month and day defaulted to 01. Coordinate corrected to the village at 47.9667, 13.0667
stops.campa: With Fritz Kohlrausch he carries instruments up into the Salzburg lake country and measures the radioactivity of the open atmosphere at Seeham, among the Trumer lakes north of the city. The method is to collect ions out of the open air and count the decay, then take the reading again hours later in weather that will not hold still. It is the last sustained experimental campaign of his life; after 1913 he works with a pen. For now there are instrument cases on a cart and a lake road running north out of Salzburg.
suggested_refs: The Schrödinger-Kohlrausch atmospheric radioactivity measurements at Seeham, 1913

segments.name: The Fortress Guns and the Broken Fortune

stops.name: Vienna, the habilitation dated into a war
stops.date_confidence: attested; MacTutor dates the habilitation degree 1 September 1914
stops.campa: The venia legendi is dated the first of September 1914, five weeks after Austria-Hungary declares war. The habilitation is the qualification an academic career in the empire turns on, the licence to lecture in one's own name. The credential arrives at a moment when there is nobody left to lecture to. He is commissioned instead into the fortress artillery. The qualification goes into a drawer and stays there four years, the whole length of the war that dissolves the state whose seal it carries. He is twenty-seven.
suggested_refs: The habilitation of 1 September 1914, University of Vienna

stops.name: Gorizia, an officer of fortress artillery
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to the place. MacTutor attests only 'Italian border (1914-1915), transferred to Hungary (1915), returned to Italian front', plus command of a battery. The specific toponyms Gorizia, Duino, Sistiana and Prosecco come from the dossier lead and are not corroborated by MacTutor or by either Wikipedia. Note also that Italy did not enter the war until May 1915, so 1914 service was on the border, not an active front; date defaulted to the month of Italian entry
stops.campa: He serves as an officer of the fortress artillery, first along the Italian border while Italy is still neutral, then on the Isonzo when it is not. The biographical lead names Gorizia among his stations, a town that eleven battles of the same river reduce to rubble. He commands a battery. Between bombardments he keeps reading theoretical physics, the one continuity between the lieutenant on the karst and the assistant who walked out of a Viennese laboratory in the summer of 1914. Whether he stood at Gorizia specifically, no military record reached here can say.
suggested_refs: Austro-Hungarian fortress artillery records of the Isonzo sector, 1915-1917, not consulted here
sources: Dossier lead, uncorroborated as to place

stops.name: Vienna, teaching meteorology in the third war spring
stops.date_confidence: attested to spring 1917 by MacTutor ('returned to Vienna spring 1917; taught meteorology course'); day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: In the spring of 1917 the army sends him back to Vienna and sets him to teach meteorology to officers. It is not the physics he wants. It is a classroom and not the Isonzo, and he takes it. He picks up contact with Exner's institute again, works on colour theory and on the statistics he had been developing before mobilization, and waits out the last eighteen months of the war within walking distance of the house he was born in. Austria-Hungary ceases to exist in November 1918.
suggested_refs: Schrödinger's wartime meteorology instruction for officers, Vienna 1917

stops.name: Salzburg, marriage to Anny Bertel
stops.date_confidence: sources disagree on the day and are not reconciled here: MacTutor gives 24 March 1920 (engagement 1919), en.wikipedia gives 6 April 1920. Both agree on the year. No venue is established in the sources reached, so the coordinate marks the Salzburg region generally, not a church or registry
stops.campa: He marries Annemarie Bertel, Anny, of a Salzburg family. The sources cannot agree on the day: one gives the twenty-fourth of March, the other the sixth of April, both in 1920. The marriage lasts forty years and produces no children. Anny keeps the household through Jena, Stuttgart, Breslau, Zürich, Berlin, Oxford, Graz, Ghent and Dublin, arranges the practicalities of two flights from fascism, and lives in the same house as the women her husband brings into it. She does not leave.
suggested_refs: The Bertel family of the Salzburg region; the wedding date conflict between MacTutor and en.wikipedia

stops.name: Jena, assistant to Max Wien
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1920 (MacTutor lists the Jena assistantship under career mobility 1920-1921, with Stuttgart following in September); month set to order the segment between the March or April wedding and the September Stuttgart post
stops.campa: He goes to Jena as assistant to Max Wien, and in the same year the Austrian Academy of Sciences awards him the Haitinger Prize. Jena lasts a matter of months. The pattern of these years is set here: a post accepted, a household packed, a better offer arriving before the boxes are unpacked. His father died in 1919 and the linoleum works is dissolving in the Austrian inflation, so there is no money behind him and no Vienna worth going home to. Postwar Germany has more physics chairs than it has physicists willing to sit in them at the salaries offered, and he takes whatever improves the position.
suggested_refs: The Haitinger Prize of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, 1920
The postwar Austrian inflation and the collapse of the Schrödinger linoleum concern
sources: en.wikipedia, 'Erwin Schrödinger', on Rudolf Schrödinger's death in 1919

stops.name: Stuttgart, extraordinary professor for a winter
stops.date_confidence: attested to September 1920 (MacTutor); day defaulted to 01. Coordinate corrected to the city-centre Keplerstrasse campus of the former Technische Hochschule, 48.7817, 9.1753
stops.campa: From September he is extraordinary professor at the Technische Hochschule in Stuttgart, a step up in title and in pay. It lasts through the winter. He is working on colour theory and on the statistical mechanics of gases, not yet on anything that will bear his name, and the papers of these years are careful and unremarkable. He is thirty-three, an age by which theoretical physicists are supposed to have done their best work. By the following spring he has accepted a full chair at Breslau.
suggested_refs: Schrödinger's colour-theory papers of the early 1920s

stops.name: Breslau, a full chair and the death of his mother
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1921 (MacTutor: chair at Breslau, then the Zürich chair accepted late in the same year; Emily Bauer's death also 1921); month set to order the segment, day defaulted
stops.campa: A full professorship at Breslau, on the eastern edge of the German-speaking world, comes in 1921 and lasts a matter of months as well. His mother Emily dies the same year. Both his parents are gone before he is thirty-four, and the Vienna he might have gone home to is a hungry provincial capital of a country a fraction of its former size. He publishes on gas theory and on specific heats, teaches the syllabus, and gives no sign to anyone in the faculty that he is anything other than a capable Austrian who has been shifted about too much. Before the year is out an offer arrives from Switzerland.
suggested_refs: The University of Breslau chair, held for months in 1921

stops.name: Zürich, the chair of theoretical physics
stops.date_confidence: attested to late 1921 (MacTutor: 'accepted theoretical physics chair in Zürich late 1921'); month and day set to order the segment
stops.campa: Zürich ends the wandering: six years in one city, the longest he stays anywhere between the Gymnasium and Dublin. Hermann Weyl is along the corridor with the mathematics Schrödinger will shortly need, and Peter Debye is across the city at the Federal Institute. He is often ill in these years. The tuberculosis that will eventually kill him is already established, and the Alpine sanatoria go into the calendar as a fixed expense, a few weeks at altitude booked between one term and the next.
suggested_refs: The University of Zürich physics chair, 1921-1927; Schrödinger's collaboration with Hermann Weyl

stops.name: Zürich, reading de Broglie
stops.date_confidence: attested to November 1925 (MacTutor: 'read de Broglie's thesis (November 1925)', and the letter to Einstein of the same month); day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: A doctoral thesis by a French aristocrat, Louis de Broglie, argues that matter has a wavelength. Schrödinger reads it in November and writes to Einstein about it within days. He is thirty-eight, a competent physicist with no great result to his name, and he has just been handed the one idea he knows exactly what to do with. If matter is a wave, then something must be waving and something must govern it. He takes the question of what equation such waves obey with him into the Christmas holiday.
stops.quote: A few days ago I read with great interest the ingenious thesis of Louis de Broglie...
stops.quote_source: Schrödinger, letter to Albert Einstein, November 1925, quoted in the MacTutor biography (truncated with an ellipsis in the source page itself)
suggested_refs: Louis de Broglie, 'Recherches sur la théorie des quanta' (1924)
The Einstein-Schrödinger correspondence, November 1925

stops.name: Arosa, the winter equation
stops.date_confidence: the Arosa holiday is attested to Christmas and New Year 1925-26 (en.wikipedia); the day is set to Christmas to place the stop within that fortnight. The companion is unidentified in the record; the Arosa detail and the companion come through Moore's biography, which this research could not open directly
stops.campa: He spends the Christmas and New Year holiday at Arosa in the Grisons, eighteen hundred metres up, a resort he already knows from taking cures there. Anny stays in Zürich. The companion who goes with him is not named in any record that survives. What comes down from the mountain in January is a wave equation whose stationary solutions reproduce the hydrogen spectrum: the discrete energy levels of the atom falling out as the resonances of a standing wave, rather than being imposed on the orbits by decree.
suggested_refs: Walter Moore, Schrödinger: Life and Thought (1989), on the Arosa holiday
The Villa Herwig at Arosa

stops.name: Zürich, Quantisierung als Eigenwertproblem
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1926 (MacTutor, en.wikipedia); the four installments run through the year in Annalen der Physik and the date is defaulted to the start of the sequence
stops.campa: Four installments under one title, 'Quantisierung als Eigenwertproblem', appear in the Annalen der Physik across a single year. Quantization stops being a rule imposed on orbits from outside and becomes what it is for a vibrating string: the eigenvalue condition of a boundary problem. In a further paper he shows that his wave mechanics and the matrix mechanics of Heisenberg, Born and Jordan, which had reached the same spectra by an unrecognizably different route, are the same theory. The Physical Review carries an English account of it the same year.
suggested_refs: Schrödinger, 'Quantisierung als Eigenwertproblem', Annalen der Physik (1926), four parts
Schrödinger, 'An Undulatory Theory of the Mechanics of Atoms and Molecules', Physical Review (1926)

stops.name: Zürich, the tutoring of Itha Junger
stops.date_confidence: en.wikipedia gives 'around 1926, at the age of 39', and he turned thirty-nine only in August 1926, so the honest range is 1926-27; month and day set within that range. The age at which the relationship became sexual is disputed and is not resolved here: seventeen per Moore's biography, nineteen per Junger's own account, with sources also giving twenty. Relayed through en.wikipedia's and de.wikipedia's summaries of Moore, whose text was not opened
stops.campa: He takes on the tutoring of a fourteen-year-old girl, Itha Junger, in mathematics. The tutoring becomes a sexual relationship. Moore's biography, working from Schrödinger's own diaries, puts her age at seventeen when it begins; Junger's own account puts it at nineteen; other sources say twenty. The sources conflict on the age. None of them disputes that it happened, and it is not an isolated episode. He kept the diaries, in his own hand, across decades, and they were read after his death.
suggested_refs: Walter Moore, Schrödinger: Life and Thought (1989), drawing on the diaries
de.wikipedia, 'Erwin Schrödinger', on the conflict over Itha Junger's age

stops.name: Copenhagen, at Bohr's institute
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to date. The visit is dated autumn 1926 in the text of heisenberg.journey.json, though that file's own stop for it carries the date field 1926-05-01 (Heisenberg's return to Copenhagen); the discrepancy is flagged, not resolved. Not independently re-verified against a Bohr-institute record
stops.campa: He travels to Blegdamsvej at Niels Bohr's invitation and the argument runs for days. Bohr will not give up the quantum jump; Schrödinger insists the jumps are an artifact and that a continuous wave picture can carry the whole of the physics. Bohr pursues him question by question until the visitor takes to his bed exhausted, and Werner Heisenberg carries the interrogation on at the bedside. Nobody concedes anything. He goes back to Zürich still holding that the jumps are not real.
suggested_refs: Bohr's Institute for Theoretical Physics, Blegdamsvej 17, Copenhagen
sources: Dossier account of the 1926 Copenhagen visit

stops.name: Brussels, the Fifth Solvay Conference
stops.date_confidence: attested; three existing journey files independently place Schrödinger at the Fifth Solvay Conference of 24 October 1927 (dirac, einstein, wolfgang_pauli). Coordinate inherited byte-identical from dirac.journey.json and einstein.journey.json; wolfgang_pauli.journey.json gives 50.8175 for the same node and niels_bohr.journey.json gives 50.841, 4.379, both flagged and not reconciled here
stops.campa: The Fifth Solvay Conference meets at the Institut de Physiologie in the Parc Leopold, on electrons and photons, and the group photograph taken there is reproduced for the next hundred years. Schrödinger sits among them. Albert Einstein spends the sessions and the breakfasts building thought experiments against the new interpretation and Niels Bohr answers each one by evening. Wave mechanics is one year old and everyone in the room already calculates with it. He had taken up Planck's chair in Berlin three weeks earlier.
suggested_refs: The 1927 Solvay group photograph, Institut de Physiologie Solvay, Parc Leopold, Brussels

stops.name: Berlin, succeeding Max Planck
stops.date_confidence: attested; MacTutor gives 1 October 1927 for taking up Planck's chair, and the Matteucci Medal in the same year
stops.campa: On the first of October he takes up the chair of theoretical physics at the Friedrich Wilhelm University, succeeding Max Planck, who wanted him for it. It is the most prestigious post in German physics. It puts him in the same city as Albert Einstein, whom he has been writing to for two years, and in the standing company of the Wednesday colloquium, with Planck and Max von Laue in the room. The Matteucci Medal arrives the same year. He has moved house four times in seven years. He buys furniture.
suggested_refs: The Berlin physics colloquium of the Planck-Einstein-von Laue years
The Matteucci Medal, 1927

stops.name: Berlin, one theory written twice
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1932 (john_von_neumann.journey.json, Berlin stop, for the publication of Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik); month and day defaulted to 01. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from that file's Berlin pin
stops.campa: John von Neumann, in the same city, publishes 'Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik' and settles by axiom what the physicists had settled by calculation: Heisenberg's matrices and Schrödinger's waves are one theory written twice, two representations of operators on a Hilbert space. The formalism that results is the one taught ever afterward, and it belongs to nobody in particular. Schrödinger's wave function enters it as a vector in that space. Whether the wave is a thing in the world or a device for computing probabilities is not a question the axioms answer, and he spends the rest of his life insisting on the first.
suggested_refs: John von Neumann, Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik (1932)

stops.name: Berlin, leaving without being pushed
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1933 (MacTutor: 'fled Germany 1933 due to Nazi persecution of Jews; arrived Oxford November 4, 1933'); the month is set to order the stop before the attested Oxford arrival, no departure date having been established in the sources reached
stops.campa: Hitler becomes chancellor in January and by spring the civil service law is emptying the universities of Jewish and politically suspect academics. Schrödinger is neither Jewish nor politically active. No law touches him and no official asks him to go. He goes. He resigns the most prestigious chair in German physics at forty-five with nothing arranged beyond an approach from Frederick Lindemann at Oxford, no post named and no salary agreed. Most of the colleagues who could have left on the same terms stay.
suggested_refs: The Law for the Restoration of the Professional Civil Service, April 1933, and the emptying of the German universities

stops.name: Oxford, Fellow of Magdalen
stops.date_confidence: attested; MacTutor gives the Oxford arrival as 4 November 1933
stops.campa: He arrives at Oxford on the fourth of November and is made a Fellow of Magdalen College. Within a month the Nobel Prize is announced. The college does not know what to make of him: no laboratory, no students of his own, no tutorial work he wants, and a household it finds impossible, since he has brought Anny and also Hildegunde March, the wife of his colleague Arthur March, who is carrying his child. The fellowship is a rescue placement. It never becomes a chair.
suggested_refs: Magdalen College, Oxford, and Frederick Lindemann's rescue placements of 1933

stops.name: Stockholm, the prize shared with Dirac
stops.date_confidence: attested; dirac.journey.json and heisenberg.journey.json both give the ceremony as 10 December 1933 at the Stockholm Concert Hall, with the delayed 1932 prize to Heisenberg conferred at the same event. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from those two files. Nobelprize.org returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch and could not be used to reconfirm
stops.campa: He receives the Nobel Prize in Physics for 1933 jointly with Paul Dirac, for the discovery of new productive forms of atomic theory. The same ceremony confers on Werner Heisenberg the prize for 1932, held over a year, so that three of the men who built quantum mechanics stand together on one stage before the Swedish court, in the first December of the National Socialist state, which one of them has already left. Schrödinger lectures on the fundamental idea of wave mechanics.
stops.quote: We are never in a position to say what really is or what really happens, but we can only say what will be observed in any concrete individual case.
stops.quote_source: Schrödinger, Nobel lecture, 'The Fundamental Idea of Wave Mechanics', 12 December 1933, quoted on Wikiquote
suggested_refs: The Nobel lecture of 12 December 1933, 'The Fundamental Idea of Wave Mechanics'

stops.name: Oxford, the birth of Ruth March
stops.date_confidence: attested; MacTutor gives 'daughter Ruth born May 30, 1934, in Oxford'
stops.campa: Ruth Georgie Erica March is born in Oxford, daughter of Erwin Schrödinger and Hildegunde March, and is raised as the daughter of Arthur March, who gives her his name. Three adults and an infant keep one household and make no particular secret of the arrangement, which is the part Oxford cannot forgive. Anny stays. She has no children of her own and will not have any. Two more daughters will be born to Schrödinger in Dublin, by two other women, in the same open manner.
suggested_refs: The Schrödinger-March household at Oxford, 1933-1936

stops.name: Princeton, the offer refused
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1934 (MacTutor: 'visiting lecturer; offered permanent position but declined'; en.wikipedia concurs); month and day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: He crosses to Princeton to lecture and is expected to stay. The offer is the one an exile in his position should take with both hands: money, permanence, an institute already gathering the best physicists the emigration is producing. He declines it. Why he declines is not settled: the secondary literature offers the household of three adults and an infant, which Princeton would have had to be told about, and offers other reasons besides. He gave none in writing that has been reached here. He goes back to England.
suggested_refs: Princeton University and the Institute for Advanced Study in the emigration years

stops.name: Oxford, the cat in the steel chamber
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1935 (MacTutor; the three-part paper appears in Naturwissenschaften that year, following the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen paper of the same year); month and day defaulted to 01. The Naturwissenschaften text was not re-fetched in full here; the cat passage is quoted from Trimmer's 1980 translation as given on Wikipedia
stops.campa: Albert Einstein, Boris Podolsky and Nathan Rosen publish a paper arguing that quantum mechanics cannot be a complete description of reality. Schrödinger answers in three parts in Naturwissenschaften, coins the word Verschränkung, entanglement, for the correlation that does the work, and builds the apparatus that outlives every argument around it: a cat, a steel chamber, one decaying atom, a hammer, a flask of prussic acid. The device is a reductio. It is meant to show that the formalism cannot be read literally at that scale.
stops.quote: A cat is put in a steel chamber along with the following infernal device...
stops.quote_source: Schrödinger, 'Die gegenwärtige Situation in der Quantenmechanik' (1935), trans. John D. Trimmer (1980), as quoted on Wikipedia
suggested_refs: Einstein, Podolsky and Rosen, 'Can Quantum-Mechanical Description of Physical Reality Be Considered Complete?' (1935)
Ursula K. Le Guin's 1974 story 'Schrödinger's Cat', which carried the image out of physics and into general culture

segments.name: Graz, the Recantation, and the Flight

stops.name: Graz, the chair in Austria
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1936 (MacTutor: an Edinburgh chair was offered in 1936 and a delayed work permit prompted acceptance of Graz instead, held 1936-1938); month and day set to the start of an academic year
stops.campa: He takes the chair at Graz. Edinburgh had offered him one and the work permit had been slow; Graz is the offer that arrives while he waits, and Graz is in Austria, which is what he wants. Austria in 1936 is still independent of Germany and under steady pressure from it, and everyone in the building knows which way the pressure runs. He had walked out of Berlin in 1933 while it was still a choice. He moves the household back inside the German-speaking world in October 1936.
suggested_refs: The University of Graz chair, 1936-1938, and the declined Edinburgh offer

stops.name: Graz, the statement in the newspaper
stops.date_confidence: attested to the weeks after the March 1938 Anschluss (en.wikipedia; the text is quoted in MacTutor); the exact date of publication is not established in the sources reached and the month is set to order the stop between the Anschluss and the August dismissal
stops.campa: German troops cross the border in March and Austria ceases to exist as a state. Schrödinger, whose 1933 departure from Berlin is on the record and known to the new authorities, publishes a statement recanting it: that he had misjudged the true will and the true destiny of his country, and that he makes the confession willingly and joyfully. He is fifty, a Nobel laureate, and he is trying to keep a job. Neither the newspaper that printed it nor the date of publication is established in any source reached here.
stops.quote: ...misjudged up to the last the true will and the true destiny of my country. I make this confession willingly and joyfully...
stops.quote_source: Schrödinger's public statement after the Anschluss, 1938, quoted in the MacTutor biography (elided at both ends in the source page)
suggested_refs: The Graz newspaper statement of spring 1938 and its reception among emigre physicists

stops.name: Graz, dismissed for political unreliability
stops.date_confidence: attested; MacTutor gives the dismissal as 26 August 1938
stops.campa: On the twenty-sixth of August he is dismissed from Graz for political unreliability. The statement bought him nothing. The position of the authorities is that a man who left Berlin in 1933 cannot be trusted, whatever he prints in a newspaper five years later. He is fifty-one, a Nobel laureate without a post, holding papers issued by a state that no longer exists, and the recantation stays on the record, quoted against him for the rest of his life and after it. He and Anny begin arranging to leave the country.
suggested_refs: The dismissal notice of 26 August 1938, University of Graz

stops.name: Rome, out through Italy
stops.date_confidence: attested that he fled to Rome after the August 1938 dismissal (MacTutor); the month is inferred from that sequence and the day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: He and Anny leave Austria for Italy with what they can carry, and reach Rome. The Pontifical Academy of Sciences, of which he is a member, sits in that city, and the membership is one of the few institutional attachments he holds that no government in Europe can cancel. From Rome the route runs back to Oxford, insecurely, and then on to Belgium. He is travelling on the papers of a country annexed six months ago, and he has no post waiting anywhere.
suggested_refs: Schrödinger's membership of the Pontifical Academy of Sciences

stops.name: Ghent, a year on the Francqui foundation
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1938-1939 (MacTutor: visiting professorship at the University of Ghent through the Fondation Francqui); month and day set to order the stop after the September flight through Rome
stops.campa: A one-year visiting professorship arranged through the Fondation Francqui gives him a desk at the University of Ghent. It is a stipend that expires in twelve months, in a country invaded within living memory by the army now massing again. Then a letter comes from Dublin. Éamon de Valera, mathematician turned head of government, is legislating an institute for advanced studies and wants Schrödinger to run its school of theoretical physics. Visas are obtained for Anny, and for Hilde March and her daughter.
stops.quote: I wanted to remain free - and could not do so without great duplicity.
stops.quote_source: Schrödinger, letter to Albert Einstein, c.1939, quoted in the MacTutor biography
suggested_refs: The Fondation Francqui appointment at Ghent, 1938-1939
De Valera's invitation and the Irish visas of 1939

segments.name: Dublin: the Institute, the Cell, the Affine Field

stops.name: Dublin, arrival in the first autumn of the war
stops.date_confidence: attested to October 1939 (MacTutor: 'moved to Dublin autumn 1939'); day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: He reaches Dublin in October, five weeks after the war begins, on a visa issued at the personal instance of the Taoiseach. Ireland is neutral and stays neutral; the man who has now left a German state twice will spend the war in the one European capital where nothing is bombed and the streetlights stay on. He is fifty-two. The institute that is to employ him has been drafted into legislation but not yet housed, and for the first months there is a salary and an intention and no building.
suggested_refs: Éamon de Valera's plan for a Dublin institute modelled on Princeton

stops.name: Clontarf, the house on Kincora Road
stops.date_confidence: attested that he lived on Kincora Road, Clontarf, through the Dublin years and that a plaque marks the residence (en.wikipedia); no house number is given in any source reached, so the coordinate marks the street. The year is set at the start of the Dublin residence and the day defaulted. Note that the research pool carried two different coordinates for this street, 550 metres apart; this file uses one value throughout
stops.campa: The household settles on Kincora Road in Clontarf, on the north shore of Dublin Bay, in a modest house that later carries a plaque. He cycles between the house and the institute and becomes a known figure in the city. Two more daughters are born to him in Dublin, by two women neither of whom is his wife, and Anny remains his wife and remains in the house. He is there seventeen years, after two decades in which he never unpacked. No source reached gives the house number.
suggested_refs: The commemorative plaque at Schrödinger's Clontarf residence, Kincora Road, Dublin

stops.name: Merrion Square, the School of Theoretical Physics
stops.date_confidence: the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies was established by the Institute for Advanced Studies Act signed 19 June 1940, but Schrödinger moved into 65 Merrion Square in February 1941 (en.wikipedia, 'Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies'); the legislative founding and his working presence are distinguished here and the stop is dated to the latter. Day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: In February 1941 he moves into 65 Merrion Square as founding director of the School of Theoretical Physics. The institute was created by an act signed the previous June, modelled openly on Princeton, and it is de Valera's own project: a small state with no money for laboratories can still afford theorists, who need paper and a room. Schrödinger runs the seminars and brings in refugee physicists from the continent. The unified field theory he starts on in this building will occupy him for the next twenty years.
suggested_refs: The Institute for Advanced Studies Act 1940; 64-65 Merrion Square, Dublin

stops.name: Dublin, Dirac comes to the institute
stops.date_confidence: attested by dirac.journey.json, which places Dirac's 1942 visit to Schrödinger at the DIAS premises on Burlington Road and supplies this coordinate, inherited here byte-identical. Other sources place the institute at Merrion Square in the same period; the address discrepancy is flagged, not resolved. Month and day as given in that file
stops.campa: Paul Dirac comes to Dublin to see him, nine years after the two of them shared a platform in Stockholm. Dirac finds his co-laureate running a school of theoretical physics for a neutral government out of a Georgian house, in a city where the war is a rumour carried by newspapers. The two of them had shared the prize for a theory neither of them could interpret to the other's satisfaction, and they take the argument up again where it was left. Dirac lectures at the institute and goes back to Cambridge.
suggested_refs: The DIAS premises on Burlington Road, Dublin, named in the record of Dirac's 1942 visit

stops.name: Trinity College Dublin, the What Is Life? lectures
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 1943 (en.wikipedia, 'What Is Life?'); day defaulted to 01. The research pool carried two coordinates for Trinity College, 53.3441/-6.2577 and 53.3438/-6.2546; the second is used throughout this file
stops.campa: Under the institute's auspices he gives public lectures at Trinity College on a question no physicist is supposed to ask: what is life. He argues that the chromosome must carry its instructions in something like an aperiodic crystal, a structure whose order does not repeat, and that a living organism holds off decay by feeding on order rather than merely on energy. Cambridge publishes the lectures the following year as What Is Life? The Physical Aspect of the Living Cell.
stops.quote: In physics we have dealt hitherto only with periodic crystals.
stops.quote_source: Schrödinger, What Is Life? The Physical Aspect of the Living Cell (Cambridge University Press, 1944), quoted on Wikiquote
suggested_refs: What Is Life? The Physical Aspect of the Living Cell (Cambridge, 1944), since translated into at least sixteen languages
The 1953 letter from Francis Crick to Schrödinger acknowledging the book's influence, held at DIAS
The annual 'What Is Life?' lecture series at Trinity College Dublin, running since 1995

stops.name: Dawson Street, the Affine Field Theory
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1947 (en.wikipedia: 'in 1947, he announced a result, Affine Field Theory'), announced to the Royal Irish Academy at 19 Dawson Street with de Valera present and heavy press coverage; the dossier's description of it as a press conference is corrected here. Month and day defaulted to 01. The 1947 newspaper accounts were not fetched directly; the quotation reaches this file through MacTutor
stops.campa: He announces to the Royal Irish Academy in Dawson Street a result he calls Affine Field Theory, presented as the generalisation that makes Einstein's own theory a special case of his. The Taoiseach is in the room. The Irish papers run it as a national event, a Nobel laureate on Irish soil superseding the most famous physicist alive. Einstein, sent the work, states publicly that the claim is premature and the theory unsupported. He is right; the affine programme produces no physics. Schrödinger keeps at it for the next fourteen years.
stops.quote: This is the generalisation. Now the Einstein Theory becomes simply a special case... I believe I am right, I shall look an awful fool if I am wrong.
stops.quote_source: Schrödinger to the Irish Times on the 1947 announcement, quoted in the MacTutor biography
suggested_refs: The Royal Irish Academy, 19 Dawson Street, Dublin
Paul Halpern, Einstein's Dice and Schrödinger's Cat, on the 1947 episode

stops.name: Dublin, Nature and the Greeks
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1954 for the publication (MacTutor); month and day defaulted to 01. The pool placed the book ambiguously between Dublin and Vienna; he is directing the Dublin institute in 1954 and the stop is pinned there. The lecture text itself was not fetched
stops.campa: He publishes Nature and the Greeks, and the argument is that the Ionians took two decisions the West has never revisited: that nature is comprehensible, and that the observer must be kept out of what is observed. The first decision made science possible. The second, he says, is the source of the trouble physics is now in, because it removes the mind from a world the mind is then asked to explain. He has been an Irish citizen since 1948 and has kept his Austrian nationality as well.
stops.quote: We do not belong to this material world that science constructs for us. We are not in it; we are outside.
stops.quote_source: Schrödinger, Nature and the Greeks (Cambridge University Press, 1954), quoted on Wikiquote
suggested_refs: Nature and the Greeks (Cambridge, 1954)
Schrödinger's Irish naturalization of 1948, taken without renouncing Austrian citizenship

stops.name: Merrion Square, retirement from the institute
stops.date_confidence: sources conflict and are not reconciled here: en.wikipedia has the DIAS post 'held until his retirement in 1955', MacTutor has 'he retired in 1956 when he returned to Vienna'. The stop is dated to the earlier of the two and the disagreement recorded. Month and day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: He retires from the institute after sixteen years, once the pension and the Austrian settlement are finally arranged. The sources differ by a year over when: one says 1955, another 1956, the year the Vienna chair begins. Neither corroborates the other and the question is left open here. Ireland had taken him in 1939, when the offers had run out, and kept him through a war and eleven years of peace. He is sixty-eight, and he is going back to Austria.
suggested_refs: The retirement date conflict between en.wikipedia (1955) and MacTutor (1956)

segments.name: Vienna Again, and the Stone at Alpbach

stops.name: Vienna, the chair made for him
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1956 (MacTutor: returned to Vienna 1956, to a specially created chair, and received the first Erwin Schrödinger Prize of the Austrian Academy of Sciences in the same year); month and day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: The University of Vienna creates a chair for him and he comes back to it, fifty years after he first walked into the building as a student of Exner and Hasenöhrl. The Austrian Academy of Sciences institutes a prize in his name and gives him the first one, folding the returned exile back into the establishment that had let him go twice. He lectures on quantum theory to students who were not born when he wrote the equation. His health is poor and the sanatoria are back in the calendar.
suggested_refs: The Erwin Schrödinger Prize of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, first awarded 1956

stops.name: Vienna, the lectures read for him
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1958 for the publication of Mind and Matter (en.wikipedia); month and day defaulted to 01. The Tarner Lectures behind the book were given in his name at Trinity College, Cambridge, in 1956 but were read on his behalf by Professor J. Wisdom, Schrödinger being too ill to travel (Wikipedia's list of Tarner Lecturers); this stop therefore stands at Vienna, where he was, and not at Cambridge, where the text was read
stops.campa: Mind and Matter appears, worked up from the Tarner Lectures given in his name at Cambridge under the title 'The physical basis of consciousness'. He did not deliver them. He was too ill to travel and the philosopher John Wisdom read the text aloud in a hall its author never entered. The book argues out of the Upanishads that consciousness is singular and its plural an appearance, and that the physicist's habit of excluding the observer is a convenience that has been mistaken for a fact about the world.
stops.quote: The world is given to me only once, not one existing and one perceived. Subject and object are only one.
stops.quote_source: Schrödinger, Mind and Matter (Cambridge University Press, 1958), quoted on Wikiquote
suggested_refs: Mind and Matter (Cambridge, 1958), ch. 4, 'The Arithmetical Paradox: The Oneness of Mind'
The 1956 Tarner Lectures, Trinity College, Cambridge, read by Professor J. Wisdom

stops.name: Vienna-Alsergrund, death
stops.date_confidence: attested; de.wikipedia gives death on 4 January 1961 in Vienna-Alsergrund of tuberculosis, corroborated by MacTutor
stops.campa: He dies of tuberculosis in the Alsergrund district of Vienna on the fourth of January, seventy-three years old, in the city he was born in. The disease had been in him since the Zürich years at least and had drawn the map of his life as much as any appointment did: Arosa, the Tyrol, the cure between terms, the winter holidays at altitude. The last book he prepared, a German volume of essays called Meine Weltansicht, appears in the year of his death.
stops.quote: This life of yours which you are living is not merely a piece of this entire existence, but in a certain sense the whole.
stops.quote_source: Schrödinger, My View of the World, trans. Cecily Hastings (Cambridge University Press, 1964), quoted on Wikiquote
suggested_refs: Meine Weltansicht (1961) and its posthumous English translation, My View of the World (1964)

stops.name: Alpbach, the equation on the stone
stops.date_confidence: the burial at Alpbach is attested (de.wikipedia, MacTutor) and follows the death of 4 January 1961; the exact date of interment is not established in the sources reached and the day is set to order the stop. Coordinate corrected to the village itself, 47.3985, 11.9439; the research pool carried two other values for this grave, both roughly one to two kilometres off
stops.campa: He is buried in the churchyard at Alpbach in the Tyrol, a village where he had taken holidays for years. He was not a Catholic and the ground is Catholic ground. The priest allows the burial on learning that the dead man belonged to the Pontifical Academy of Sciences, which is how a lifelong unbeliever ends up under a consecrated hillside. The headstone carries no cross and no scripture. It carries the equation, in its time-dependent form, cut into the stone.
suggested_refs: The grave at Alpbach, Tyrol, inscribed with the time-dependent Schrödinger equation

stops.name: Vienna, the face on the banknote
stops.date_confidence: posthumous. Attested: the bust in the Arkadenhof of the University of Vienna, the portrait on the Austrian 1000-schilling note issued 1983-1997, the lunar far-side crater, and the Erwin Schrödinger International Institute (en.wikipedia). The institute's founding year is disputed: en.wikipedia gives 1992, the institute's own site says it opened in 1993; both are recorded. Date set to the earlier year, day and month defaulted
stops.campa: A bust of him goes up in the arcaded courtyard of the University of Vienna, among the professors the institution decided to keep. His face is printed on the thousand-schilling note from 1983 until the schilling is retired, the second highest denomination the republic issues. A crater on the far side of the Moon carries his name. Vienna charters an international institute for mathematics and physics in his name, which opens the following year and is still working.
suggested_refs: The Erwin Schrödinger International Institute for Mathematics and Physics, Vienna
The Austrian 1000-schilling note, 1983-1997
The lunar crater Schrödinger

stops.name: Trinity College Dublin, the name comes off the theatre
stops.date_confidence: posthumous. Attested to January 2022 (en.wikipedia): the Trinity physics department recommended renaming a lecture theatre that had carried his name since the 1990s and reconsidering the eponymous lecture series. The underlying diary evidence reaches this file through Moore's biography as summarized on Wikipedia and through the 2021 Irish Times investigation, neither of which was opened directly here. Day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: The physics department at Trinity College Dublin recommends taking his name off a lecture theatre that had carried it since the 1990s, and reconsidering the lecture series named for him. The occasion is a renewed public reading of his diaries: the tutoring of Itha Junger from the age of fourteen, an infatuation with a girl of twelve, a pattern of pursuit recorded in his own hand across decades. No charge was ever brought against him in his lifetime and no trial ever took place. The recommendation is dated January 2022.
suggested_refs: The 2021 Irish Times investigation into Schrödinger's conduct
Walter Moore, Schrödinger: Life and Thought (1989), the source of the diary material
